referents.why: 'Our' unrighteousness: first plural, the speakers 'we'; no candidate is first plural.
referents.category: speaker group not offered as candidate

referents.why: Interrogative 'what' (neuter singular) in 'what shall we say?'; refers to no candidate.
'We' who say (first plural): the speakers of the diatribe, not a candidate; the builder's w0 is not a candidate.
referents.category: speaker group not offered as candidate

referents.why: 'I speak' (first singular): the writer Paul in a parenthetical; not a candidate.
referents.category: writer's own voice not offered as candidate

links.why: Reversed: the question 'what shall we say?' (cl0) is what the condition governs, not the other way round.
The if-clause cl1 ('if our unrighteousness shows God's righteousness') conditions the question cl0; cl0 carries the 'if' opener.
'The one inflicting the wrath' is an articular participle describing God in cl2, not a clause joined by and to the question.
The articular participle is nested in cl2 as the description of God, the role of a relative clause in a noun phrase.
links.category: descriptive participle nested in noun phrase

links.why: 'What shall we say?' is a saying clause; 'That God is unjust ...?' is what is said (R1).

groups.why: The condition 'if our unrighteousness shows God's righteousness' governs 'what shall we say?'.
The saying 'what shall we say?' with what is said, 'God unjust?'. No sender is offered, so none is recorded.

none_fit.what: A parenthetical qualifier of the writer's own speech; no link type records it, so it is left unlinked.

cant_tell.what: Sender of the turn (the 'we' of 'what shall we say?')
cant_tell.why: The 'we' is the diatribe's speaker and is not offered as a candidate; the turn has no sender.
Contrast with a verse-opening 'but' has no host in its own verse; no link added.
